initial_observation.demographics: 48-year-old man, known to have diabetes mellitus and ulcerative colitis
initial_observation.encounter_context: referred to hospital with complaints of moderate pain in the right upper-quadrant area for 1 month
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: Presented with intermittent right upper-quadrant pain for 1 month, fatigue, constipation for 6 days, and significant weight loss of approximately 18 kg over 1 month. No nausea, vomiting, anorexia, rectal bleeding, gallstones, or jaundice. Physical examination showed a palpable mass in the epigastric region, no pallor or jaundice, vitally stable and afebrile. Rectal exam revealed an empty rectum. Laboratory investigations and tumor markers were normal.
presenting_symptoms: weight loss of approximately 18 kg over 1 month
known_prior_history: diabetes mellitus on oral hypoglycemic agent
ulcerative colitis controlled with Azathioprine, no flare-ups in past six years
family history: father had lung cancer
no history of smoking or alcohol intake

evidence_items.source_text: A contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis was performed at the referring hospital, and it showed a segment of circumferential wall thickening affecting the proximal descending colon, 6.3 cm long, with a maximum wall thickness of 1.6 cm. Peri-colonic fat stranding and multifocal regional nodules and lymph nodes were identified. Multiple peritoneal deposits were seen, and the largest deposit was seen along the mesenteric margin, measuring 4.9×3 cm. There was no definitive involvement of adjacent structures. There were innumerable hypovascular ring-enhancing hepatic masses scattered in both lobes involving all liver segments, and the largest was located at segment 4b, measuring 8.1 cm. There was also necrotic lymphadenopathy seen at the gastrohepatic ligament. The lungs were clear, with no suspicious pulmonary nodules
A full colonoscopy showed circumferential wall thickening, from which a biopsy was taken, and stenting over the area of the thickening secondary to the tumor was done

Histopathological examination of the descending colon biopsy demonstrated dual morphologies in which a predominant component comprised of tumor cells arranged in nested, organoid, and rosette-like growth patterns with a focal area of solid sheet associated with brisk mitotic activity estimated at 30 mitotic figures per 10 high-powered fields (Figure 3A). The second minor component (30%) exhibited intermingled malignant glandular structures morphologically consistent with adenocarcinoma (Figure 3B). The predominant component was diffusely positive for Pancytokeratin (AE1/AE3) and Synaptophysin and negative for Chromogranin immunohisto-chemical stains, whereas adenocarcinoma was negative for the neuroendocrine markers (Figure 3C, 3D).

The patient was therefore diagnosed with metastatic poorly differentiated MANEC of the colon, which was deemed unresectable. It had metastasized to the liver with multiple peritoneal deposits based on radiological and histopathological findings.

The patient was referred to the medical oncology department, where he received a total of 9 cycles of cisplatin and etopo-side. The CT scan showed a good response to chemotherapy, with regression of the primary tumor, liver, and bony metastasis. However, he later developed right retinal vein thrombosis.

diagnostic_reasoning_verbatim_spans: Histopathological examination of the descending colon biopsy demonstrated dual morphologies in which a predominant component comprised of tumor cells arranged in nested, organoid, and rosette-like growth patterns with a focal area of solid sheet associated with brisk mitotic activity estimated at 30 mitotic figures per 10 high-powered fields. The second minor component (30%) exhibited intermingled malignant glandular structures morphologically consistent with adenocarcinoma. The predominant component was diffusely positive for Pancytokeratin (AE1/AE3) and Synaptophysin and negative for Chromogranin immunohisto-chemical stains, whereas adenocarcinoma was negative for the neuroendocrine markers. The Ki-67 proliferative index in neuroendocrine carcinoma is estimated at more than 90% by manual quantitative assessment. The diagnosis was compatible with mixed poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma of large cell type and adenocarcinoma.
